ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Mike has 125 small, equally big cubes. He glues some of them together in such a way that one big cube with exactly nine tunnels is created (see diagram). The tunnels go all the way straight through the cube. How many of the 125 cubes is he not using?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, all visible edges of the large cube are divided into 5 equal parts, so it corresponds to a 5×5×5 block of small cubes. In the figure, 9 straight-through tunnels are visible: there are 3 openings on the top face, 3 openings on the front/left visible face, and 3 openings on the right visible face; these tunnels pass through the entire large cube along three mutually perpendicular directions respectively, and the opening positions are arranged according to the corresponding diagonal-line positions. Then reason: 125=5×5×5, so if each straight-through tunnel is counted separately, it would remove 5 small cubes. For 9 tunnels, the preliminary count removes 9×5=45 small cubes. Since the three mutually perpendicular tunnels at corresponding positions intersect at the same small cube, there are 3 such triple intersections in the figure. Each triple intersection is counted 3 times in the count of 45, but actually should only be removed once, so each intersection is overcounted by 2, for a total overcount of 3×2=6. Therefore the actual number of unused small cubes is 45−6=39.

raw_record.question_text: Mike has 125 small, equally big cubes. He glues some of them together in such a way that one big cube with exactly nine tunnels is created (see diagram). The tunnels go all the way straight through the cube. How many of the 125 cubes is he not using?

method.method_draft: Use inclusion-exclusion on the nine straight tunnels. From the diagram, identify the cube as a 5 by 5 by 5 block because the text gives 125 equal small cubes and the visible edges are divided into 5 parts. Read the image as showing 3 straight tunnels in each of the three perpendicular directions: three openings on the top face, three on the front/left visible face, and three on the right visible face, arranged on corresponding diagonal positions through the interior. Each tunnel would remove 5 small cubes, so nine separate tunnels would remove 9 × 5 = 45 cubes. Then account for overlaps: the three diagonal positions make the tunnels meet in 3 triple-intersection cubes, one for each matched diagonal position. At each such cube, three tunnel counts include the same cube, so the naive total overcounts by 2 there. Total overcount is 3 × 2 = 6, so the actual number of omitted cubes is 45 − 6 = 39. Therefore Mike does not use 39 cubes.

method.method_draft: Count the missing cubes layer by layer, using horizontal slices from bottom to top. The text and image show a 5-by-5-by-5 cube. From the diagram, read the tunnels as three vertical top-to-bottom tunnels in diagonal positions, plus three horizontal tunnels in one side-to-side direction and three in the perpendicular side-to-side direction, located in the three middle height layers. In the bottom layer, only the three vertical tunnels remove cubes, so 3 cubes are missing. In each of the three middle layers, there are the three vertical missing positions, plus one full 5-cube row tunnel and one full 5-cube column tunnel crossing at one of those vertical positions; this gives 5 + 5 − 1 plus the other two vertical holes, or 11 missing cubes per middle layer. The top layer again has only the three vertical tunnel holes, so 3 cubes are missing. Total missing cubes: 3 + 11 + 11 + 11 + 3 = 39. Thus 39 of the 125 cubes are not used.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：附图显示一个由小方块组成的大立方体，顶面和侧面都可数出每条边被分成5份，所以整体是5×5×5，共125个小方块位置。图中可见隧道是笔直贯穿的：顶面有3个上下贯通的竖直洞；在中间三层里，还能看到每层各有一条横向贯穿的隧道和一条与之垂直方向的横向贯穿隧道。推理：按从下到上的5个水平层来数没有使用的小方块。最底层只有3个竖直隧道位置缺块，所以缺3块。每个中间层有一条长度为5的整行隧道和一条长度为5的整列隧道，它们交叉的1块不能重复计算，所以这两条隧道共缺5+5−1=9块；另外还有其余两个竖直洞位置，因此每个中间层缺9+2=11块。这样的中间层有3层，所以缺11+11+11块。最顶层同底层一样，只有3个竖直隧道位置缺块，所以缺3块。总共没有使用的小方块数为3+11+11+11+3=39。
